Open asks (can you confirm these by EOD tomorrow?):
1) Estimated monthly tokens (if you can break down by route: triage vs summarization vs other)

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers so we can align on a committed renewal that makes sense for Acme.

Subject: Re: Renewal/Expansion: Volume step-ups & blended rates — pricing proposal attached

Great — thanks for the details, Sam. I updated the attached workbook with two concrete scenarios and a proposed quarterly step-up schedule. Summary below: 

Pricing summary (proposed):
- Tier A: 0–49M tokens/month — list rate $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Tier B: 50–99M tokens/month — discounted rate $900 per 1M tokens
- Tier C: 100M+ tokens/month — discounted rate $700 per 1M tokens

Blended-rate examples (assumes no model-specific premiums):
- Example 1 (current mix, triage 60% / summarization 32% / misc 8%): blended = $1,056 per 1M tokens (weighted).
- Example 2 (with new routes; triage 50% / summarization 40% / long-context analytics 10%): blended = $936 per 1M tokens.

Notes on route/model effects and unit economics:
- Summarization sessions are higher token-per-session but benefit more from prefix/KV caching for repeated notes; we’ve modeled a conservative 10–20% effective token reduction for summarization flows in the workbook.
- We can implement per-route telemetry tags so billing calculates a blended rate across tagged routes automatically — Dev is cc’d to help with instrumentation details.
- Step-up mechanics: we recommend quarterly true-ups tied to committed volumes. Example ramp: Q3 commit 25M -> Q4 target 50M -> Q1 100M. Discounts apply retroactively for the quarter once the committed threshold is met (so you get the lower unit price for all usage in the quarter once threshold crossed).

Commercial incentives:
- If Acme signs a 12-month committed renewal by Aug 20, we’ll add a one-time 10% credit on the first two invoice cycles (applied as a dollar credit) to help with pilot costs.

Next steps:
1) Dev: can you confirm telemetry tagging approach and any runtime changes required to support per-route billing?
2) Sam/Priya: confirm preferred ramp schedule (quarterly targets) and I’ll draft a renewal addendum and send for initial legal review.

Attached: updated 20260810-pricing_estimate.xlsx (scenarios A/B + blended examples).

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Renewal/Expansion: Volume step-ups & blended rates — technical notes

Quick technical notes on telemetry and effective unit costs: 
- Per-route tagging: straightforward — add a route_id header or set a request tag in the SDK and we’ll emit usage events with route_id. That enables per-route reporting and blended billing. No runtime restart required.
- Token counting: we count tokens on the server-side post-tokenization; small differences across tokenizer versions are normalized in the billing pipeline.
- Caching impact: for summarization, if you reuse prefixes across requests (e.g., same patient context), KV caching can reduce compute tokens by ~10–25% depending on repetition. Workbook uses a conservative 10% reduction.
- Model variants: we can route 80% of low-latency triage to a smaller, cheaper variant and 20% to a higher-quality model for escalation. That requires model-aware routing policy (we can implement on the routing side) and will be reflected in blended billing.

I’ll work with Marissa to outline the telemetry keys and a short README for your engineers so the tagging is straightforward.

—Dev
